Preface 前言

原书第 17 页

Software architects occupy a unique space in the world of IT. They are expected to know the technologies and software platforms on which their organizations run, as well as the businesses that they serve. A great software architect needs to master both sides of the architect's coin: business and technology. This is no small challenge, and it's why this book was created.

软件架构师在 IT 世界中占据着一个独特的位置：他们既要熟悉组织赖以运转的技术与软件平台，又要理解自己所服务的业务。一名优秀的架构师需要同时掌握这枚硬币的两面——业务与技术。这绝非易事，而这也正是本书诞生的缘由。

97 Things Every Software Architect Should Know provides advice from software architects around the world on everything from how to avoid common pitfalls to how to build talented teams. It's a smorgasbord of advice from established software architects for other software architects or those who aspire to become software architects.

《97 位软件架构师应知应会的 97 件事》汇集了全球软件架构师们的建议，内容涵盖如何避开常见陷阱、如何打造有战斗力的团队等等。它是一道道由资深架构师端出的大杂烩，献给正在做架构师、以及有志于成为架构师的人。

It's my sincere hope that this book will be a source of inspiration and guidance for software professionals everywhere. It's also my hope that software architects will use this book and its sister website to share advice and insights into what is perhaps the most challenging profession in information technology today.

我衷心希望这本书能成为各地软件从业者的灵感与指南。我也希望架构师们能借助本书及其姊妹网站，彼此分享关于这个也许是当今 IT 行业最具挑战性的职业的洞见。

This book is probably completely different from any other book you've read. It is the combined work of more than four dozen authors, all of whom donated their thoughts and advice about software architecture without compensation. It is, in a way, an open source book in the truest sense. Each author wrote his or her own contributions, those contributions were examined and edited with the author, and then the best contributions were chosen for publication. That's not much different than an open source software project where individuals contribute code rather than knowledge and wisdom.

这本书大概和你读过的任何书都不一样。它由四十多位作者合力写成，所有人都无偿贡献了自己关于软件架构的思考与建议。从某种意义上说，这是一本真正意义上的开源书：每位作者独立撰写自己的篇章，与编辑一起打磨，最终择优结集出版。这和开源软件项目非常像，只不过大家贡献的不是代码，而是知识与智慧。

Permissions 授权说明

原书第 18 页

The licensing of each axiom is also similar to open source. Every contribution is freely available online and licensed under Creative Commons, Attribution 3.0, which means that you can use the individual contributions in your own work as long as you give credit to the original author. Other open source books have been tried and have, with only a few exceptions, failed. I believe that is because it's harder for individuals to contribute to a project unless it can be modularized. This book succeeds for exactly that reason: it is modularized. Each contribution is self-contained and works both in this larger collection and on its own.

每一篇短文的授权方式也类似开源：所有内容都在线免费发布，采用 CC BY 3.0（署名）协议——只要署上原作者名字，你就可以在自己的作品中引用这些篇章。过去也有人尝试做开源书，但几乎都失败了。我认为原因在于：一个项目如果不能模块化，个人就很难往里贡献。这本书之所以做成，正是因为它是模块化的——每一篇都自成一体，既可以收入合集，也可以独立成篇。

Acknowledgments 致谢

The idea for this book was not conceived in a vacuum. In order, I'd like to thank Jay Zimmerman, who suggested a talk called "10 Things Every Software Architect Should Know"; Bruce Eckel, who managed the mailing list where the idea germinated; Jeremy Meyer, who suggested turning a slide show into a book; Nitin Borwankar, who suggested a public wiki so everyone could contribute; and the members of Bruce's mailing list who, on nothing more than a promise, donated their time and wrote the first axioms. I also thank the dozens of architects whose submissions didn't make the cut — choosing was extremely hard. O'Reilly deserves credit for listening with open ears and backing an untested method of publishing a book, and for agreeing that all content be open source (CC BY 3.0) and free on the website.

这本书的想法并非凭空而来。按先后顺序，我要感谢：Jay Zimmerman，是他建议我做一场题为《软件架构师应知应会的 10 件事》的演讲；Bruce Eckel，他维护的邮件列表是本书想法的温床；Jeremy Meyer，是他建议把幻灯片扩展成一本书；Nitin Borwankar，他提议建一个公开 wiki 让所有人参与；以及 Bruce 邮件列表里那些仅凭一句承诺就贡献时间、写出最初几篇短文的成员。我还要感谢几十位投稿但最终未被收录的架构师——取舍异常艰难。O'Reilly 也值得记上一笔：他们侧耳倾听了这个想法，支持了一种未经检验的出书方式，并同意所有内容以 CC BY 3.0 协议开源、在网站上免费开放。
